title: View Market Data
description: Allow users to inspect the raw market data returned by the backend for a selected trading symbol.
acceptance: The user can select a supported trading symbol.
The UI retrieves data from GET /markets/{symbol}/market-data.
The current price is displayed.
The order book bids and asks are displayed.
All candle series grouped by timeframe are displayed.
Loading and error states are presented to the user.

title: View Market Analysis
description: Allow users to inspect the deterministic market analysis generated by the analysis engine.
acceptance: The user can select a supported trading symbol.
The UI retrieves data from GET /markets/{symbol}/analysis.
The regime assessment is displayed.
The risk assessment is displayed.
The economic assessment is displayed.
The exposure profile is displayed.
The catalog recommendation is displayed.
Loading and error states are presented to the user.

title: View Market Classification
description: Allow users to inspect the market classification signals generated from the deterministic analysis.
acceptance: The user can select a supported trading symbol.
The UI retrieves data from GET /markets/{symbol}/classification.
Regime classification signals are displayed.
Risk classification signals are displayed.
Economic classification signals are displayed.
Exposure classification signals are displayed.
Each signal shows its source, score, and reason.
Loading and error states are presented to the user.

title: App Layout
description: Provide a shared application layout that wraps product views with consistent chrome, branding, and navigation between Market Data, Analysis, and Classification.
acceptance: All product views render inside a shared application layout.
The layout shows the Market Data product brand as a primary chrome signal.
The user can navigate between Market Data, Analysis, and Classification views from the layout.
The active view is visually indicated in the navigation.
Layout chrome remains consistent across views (header/nav structure does not change per screen).

title: Human-Readable Labels
description: Map backend DTO enum and reason-code values to human-readable UI text in the frontend mapping layer so analysis (and shared label infrastructure) displays readable copy instead of raw API tokens.
acceptance: Backend analysis regime labels (e.g. TREND_UP) are displayed as human-readable text.
Backend analysis regime reason codes are displayed as human-readable text in summaries.
Label catalogs live in locale JSON (or shared label helpers); mappers do not hardcode display English inline.
Unknown codes fall back safely without failing the entire payload mapping.
Screens continue to consume view models only; UI components do not map raw DTO codes.
Existing market analysis success, loading, and error flows remain intact.

title: Extend Human-Readable Labels
description: Extend the existing locale-backed label helpers to humanize remaining analysis and classification DTO codes shown in the UI: classification reason codes, strategy catalog tokens, and analysis component/factor key names.
acceptance: Classification regime, risk, economic, and exposure reason codes are displayed as human-readable text.
Analysis preferred strategy / catalog strategy tokens (e.g. TREND_FOLLOWING) are displayed as human-readable text.
Analysis exposure factor names (e.g. vol_budget_pct) are displayed as human-readable text.
Analysis risk and economic component names in summaries are displayed as human-readable text.
Label catalogs live in locale JSON; mappers use existing resolveLabel helpers (or thin wrappers) and do not hardcode display English inline.
Unknown codes fall back safely to the raw code without failing payload mapping.
Screens continue to consume view models only; UI components do not map raw DTO codes.
Existing analysis and classification success, loading, and error flows remain intact.

title: Content Message Contract
description: Define the Content module boundary and the stable MessageRef / ResolvedMessage schemas plus code-registry shape so catalogs and resolve can be added without redesign. Replaces ad-hoc DTO→label maps over later Content Features.
acceptance: A bounded Content module area exists in the FE package layout (clear directory/package boundary suitable for later extraction).
MessageRef is typed with at least code, optional params, optional severity, and optional channel.
ResolvedMessage is typed with at least code, locale, and text (optional meta allowed).
A code-registry shape is defined for catalog entries (semantic code id, params schema/severity metadata as designed).
Feature mappers and screens do not yet need to resolve messages; this Feature only establishes the contract and module skeleton.
Brand chrome wording via @market-data/brand remains out of scope for this module.

title: Content Catalogs v1
description: Implement v1 Content catalogs and en/ui templates with an in-process resolve API inside the Content module (depends on content-message-contract).
acceptance: Content catalogs register the message codes needed for analysis/classification narrative planned in this epic.
en locale templates exist for the ui channel for those registered codes.
resolve({ locale, channel, messages }) returns ResolvedMessage[] for valid MessageRef inputs.
Param interpolation (and basic formatters as needed for v1) produces display text from params without callers owning copy.
Missing or unknown codes fall back safely (e.g. to code or default-locale behavior) without throwing across the whole batch.
Resolve remains in-process in FE; no remote content-service is required for v1.

title: Content Resolve Boundary
description: Route app-boundary message resolution through the Content module resolve API and retire ad-hoc label SoT (analysisLabels.* and equivalent feature-local code→English maps). Depends on content-catalogs-v1. Replaces, does not patch on top of, human-readable-labels / extend-human-readable-labels catalogs as SoT.
acceptance: App mapping/boundary layer resolves user-facing narrative MessageRefs via Content resolve (locale + ui channel).
Feature-local DTO→label maps (e.g. analysisLabels.* style catalogs) are no longer the source of truth for analysis/classification narrative copy.
Unknown codes still fall back safely without failing the entire payload mapping.
Screens continue to consume view models; UI components do not own code→English maps.
Existing analysis and classification success, loading, and error flows remain intact at the boundary.

title: Analysis & Classification Copy Wiring
description: Wire analysis and classification view models to Content-resolved messages (summaries, rationale, levels as designed) so screens bind resolved strings only. Depends on content-resolve-boundary.
acceptance: Analysis view models expose resolved narrative text (or refs already resolved at the boundary) for summaries/rationale/levels covered by this epic.
Classification view models expose resolved narrative text for signal reasons and related user-facing copy covered by this epic.
Analysis and Classification screens bind resolved strings; they do not map raw MessageRef codes to English inline.
Raw API tokens or prose dumps are not shown as the primary user-facing narrative where MessageRefs are provided.
Existing analysis and classification success, loading, and error flows remain intact.

title: Reading Layout Shell
description: Present a Symbol Reading as a gray-box Region workspace (Context, Analysis, Classification, Evidence, Market Data, Diagnostics) per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md, using brand tokens/components for region chrome. Structural fidelity only — not hi-fi polish.
acceptance: A Symbol Reading surface exposes distinct Context, Analysis, Classification, Evidence, Market Data, and Diagnostics Regions (gray-box structure acceptable).
Context + Analysis are available in the initial viewport so the Symbol and primary interpretation can be grasped without scrolling for the primary message.
Analysis is the most prominent Region; Classification is compact and subordinate; Market Data and Evidence do not dominate the workspace.
Region chrome and spacing use brand tokens/components already available to the FE (no ad-hoc design system).
Layout follows knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md hierarchy and anti-patterns (no equal-weight Region wall; no Market-Data-first Reading).
Existing symbol selection, loading, and error flows remain usable for the Reading surface.

title: Reading Analysis Composition
description: Inside the Analysis Region, present gray-box Assessment peers (Regime, Risk, Economic, Exposure), Recommendation, and claim-bound Narrative per knowledge/ux/analysis-contract.md, using brand tokens/components. Depends on reading-layout-shell for the hosting Analysis Region.
acceptance: The Analysis Region contains one Assessments workspace with peer units for Regime, Risk, Economic, and Exposure (gray-box structure acceptable).
Recommendation is composed with Assessments (not a standalone primary Region) and is visible in the initial Analysis viewport without scrolling for the stance.
Narrative appears bound to Assessment/Recommendation claims — not as a detached essay Region.
No Overall Assessment / Overall Score / Synthesis Region or rollup that replaces the four Assessment dimensions.
Composition follows knowledge/ux/analysis-contract.md hierarchy and anti-patterns (interpretation before Evidence; Classification not nested as an Analysis-owned Region).
Assessment/Recommendation chrome uses brand tokens/components already available to the FE.

title: Reading App Navigation
description: Make Symbol Reading the primary product surface per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md; resolve dual IA so legacy Market Data / Analysis / Classification destinations do not compete as equal peers with the Reading workspace (subordinate or retire competing screens as specified).
acceptance: Symbol Reading is reachable as the primary way to inspect a Symbol from app chrome.
Legacy Market Data, Analysis, and Classification destinations no longer present a competing equal product IA alongside Reading (demoted, merged, or removed per specification).
Reading Regions hierarchy from knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md remains intact (Analysis primary; no Market-Data-first Reading).
Active destination / surface is visually indicated in navigation chrome.
Existing Symbol selection, loading, and error flows remain usable on the Reading surface.
User-facing nav labels use locale / brand wording — no hardcoded English in components.

title: Reading Context Identity
description: Present full Identity in the Context Region of the Symbol Reading per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md (display name / pair form — not ticker string alone), without competing with Analysis for message prominence.
acceptance: Context Region shows Identity beyond a bare ticker string (display name and/or base-quote / pair form as available).
Context does not show price, scores, signals, or recommendations.
Context remains a small frame and does not outrank Analysis for message prominence.
Identity chrome uses brand tokens/components already available to the FE.
User-facing Identity labels come from locale catalogs / brand wording.

title: Reading Evidence Composition
description: Compose the Evidence Region per knowledge/ux/evidence-contract.md: Drivers → Features → Contributions attached to claims; stop nesting assessment components/factors as Analysis-owned body. Depends on reading-layout-shell Analysis/Evidence Regions.
acceptance: Evidence Region presents claim-attached explainability using Drivers → Features → Contributions (gray-box structure acceptable).
Assessment components / exposure factors are not the primary body owned inside Assessment peers; explainability lives in Evidence (or claim-attached Evidence depth).
Users can understand Analysis outcomes without opening Evidence depth (interpretation before Evidence).
Evidence is never a free-floating metrics dashboard unrelated to a claim.
Composition follows knowledge/ux/evidence-contract.md anti-patterns (no Metrics/Observations kind labels; Market Data not labeled as Evidence until cited).
Evidence chrome uses brand tokens/components already available to the FE.

title: Reading Diagnostics
description: Wire the Diagnostics Region per knowledge/ux/diagnostics-contract.md: quiet when healthy, elevated when blocking; trust qualification without becoming the hero message. Depends on reading-layout-shell Diagnostics Region.
acceptance: Diagnostics Region is distinct and present on a successful Reading (gray-box acceptable when no active diagnostics).
When healthy, Diagnostics stay quiet / minimal and do not compete with Analysis for primary attention.
When blocking or strongly qualifying trust, Diagnostics elevate near the affected Reading and are unmistakable without replacing Analysis as the hero message.
Confidence / data-quality is not presented as an Assessment dimension inside Analysis.
Composition follows knowledge/ux/diagnostics-contract.md anti-patterns (no burying blocking Diagnostics only at page end or only inside Evidence tables).
Diagnostics chrome uses brand tokens/components already available to the FE.

title: Reading Classification Body
description: Fill the Classification Region with compact signal packaging (source, score, reason) per dimension per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md — not count-only summary; remains subordinate and adjacent to Analysis.
acceptance: Classification Region shows regime, risk, economic, and exposure signal groups (empty groups allowed).
Each displayed signal shows source, score, and reason (reason as human-readable narrative when available).
Classification remains compact and visually subordinate / adjacent to Analysis — not equal prominence.
Classification is not nested as an Analysis-owned Region inside Assessments.
Region body uses brand tokens/components already available to the FE.
User-facing labels and reasons come from locale / Content-resolved copy — no hardcoded designed English in components.

title: Reading Market Data Body
description: Fill the Market Data Region with Price, Order book, and Candles as supporting observation per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md — never the primary interpretive Region of the Symbol Reading.
acceptance: Market Data Region displays current Price for the selected Symbol.
Market Data Region displays Order book Bids and Asks.
Market Data Region displays Candles grouped by timeframe.
Market Data remains a supporting Region — not marked primary and not the first Region in the primary interpretive band.
Market Data is visually distinct from Evidence (observation ≠ explainability).
Region body uses brand tokens/components already available to the FE.

title: Dashboard App Chrome
description: Consume published `@maguer/market-data-brand@^0.2.0` and adapt AppLayout / AppShell chrome to dashboard-mockup surface fidelity: slim `AppHeaderBar` (`density="slim"`), brand mark + name, Reading-primary nav, `ThemeToggle`, optional breadcrumb, and `StatusFooter`/`LiveStatus` for date/source/Live — Symbol Reading remains the primary product surface per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md.
acceptance: FE depends on `@maguer/market-data-brand@^0.2.0` (or newer compatible) so dashboard kit exports are available.
App chrome presents a slim header via `AppHeader`/`AppHeaderBar` density="slim" with brand mark and product name as primary chrome signals.
Navigation presentation keeps Symbol Reading as the primary product surface (no resurrecting legacy peer destinations as equal IA).
Theme toggle is present and uses brand `ThemeToggle` (no ad-hoc FE theme control).
Optional breadcrumb chrome may appear; it must not reintroduce competing equal destinations.
Footer (or equivalent quiet chrome) shows date/source and Live/status via brand `StatusFooter`/`LiveStatus`.
Chrome styling uses brand tokens/CSS variables and UI components only — no second FE token set or Tailwind design system.
Existing Symbol selection, loading, and error flows remain usable on the Reading surface.
User-facing chrome labels use locale / brand wording — no hardcoded designed English in components.

title: Dashboard Hero Band
description: Compose the top Reading band to the dashboard-mockup hero using `@maguer/market-data-brand@^0.2.0`: Symbol identity (logo/pair/full name) adjacent to observation (price, change with semantic positive/negative `Text`/`Badge` tones, sparkline in `ChartFrame`/chart tokens, timeframe pills via `SegmentedControl`/`TimeframeControl`, 24H high/low/vol, last update) without making Context own scores or recommendations. Region ownership stays per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md.
acceptance: The top Reading band visually reads as one hero: identity adjacent to price observation (not a gray-box Context stub alone).
Identity content remains Context-owned (display name / pair / logo as available); Context does not own scores, signals, or recommendations.
Observation strip shows price, change, and supporting 24H/high-low/vol / last-update fields available from existing Market Data payloads.
Change emphasis uses brand semantic positive/negative tokens or `Text`/`Badge` tones — no ad-hoc FE color hex.
Sparkline chrome uses brand `ChartFrame` and/or chart CSS variables; timeframe pills use `SegmentedControl`/`TimeframeControl` — no ad-hoc FE chart chrome library.
Hero composition does not re-home Analysis interpretation or Recommendation into Context.
Surface uses `@maguer/market-data-brand` tokens and UI components only.
User-facing labels come from locale catalogs / brand wording.

title: Dashboard Analysis Cards
description: Restyle Analysis Assessment peers (Regime, Risk, Economic, Exposure) as the dashboard mockup’s four vertical cards (icon, label, badge, score, summary) using `@maguer/market-data-brand@^0.2.0` Card/Badge/Text primitives, preserving Assessment peer ownership and Recommendation rules from knowledge/ux/analysis-contract.md.
acceptance: Analysis Region presents four Assessment peers (Regime, Risk, Economic, Exposure) as vertical cards matching mockup card structure (icon, label, badge, score, summary as data allows).
Cards use `@maguer/market-data-brand/ui` Card, Badge, Text (and related) primitives — not a parallel FE card system.
No Overall Assessment / Overall Score / Synthesis Region or rollup that replaces the four Assessment dimensions.
Recommendation composition rules from knowledge/ux/analysis-contract.md remain intact (not a fifth Assessment card).
Assessment cards remain the primary interpretive surface; Classification stays out of Analysis ownership.
Existing analysis loading and error flows remain usable.

title: Dashboard Observation Row
description: Restyle the Market Data Region as the dashboard-mockup middle observation row using `@maguer/market-data-brand@^0.2.0`: price area chart framed with `ChartFrame` (left) + Market Stats 24H card (right), with timeframe controls via `SegmentedControl`/`TimeframeControl`. Market Data remains supporting observation per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md.
acceptance: Market Data Region layout presents a chart panel and a Market Stats 24H panel as a middle observation row (not a gray-box metric dump).
Price/area chart chrome uses brand `ChartFrame` and chart CSS variables (`--chart-*`) — no second FE chart design system; plotting stays consumer-owned inside the frame.
Market Stats 24H card shows available 24H stats (e.g. high/low/volume) from existing payloads using brand Card/Text primitives.
Timeframe controls use brand `SegmentedControl`/`TimeframeControl`.
Market Data remains a supporting Region — not the primary interpretive Region and not marked as Evidence.
Surface uses `@maguer/market-data-brand` tokens and UI components only.
Existing Market Data loading and error flows remain usable.

title: Dashboard Classification Surface
description: Restyle the Classification Region as the dashboard-mockup Factor/Score/Reason table (and compact score visualization if needed) using `@maguer/market-data-brand@^0.2.0` Table/Card/Text — without inventing an Overall Assessment / Synthesis rollup that replaces the four Analysis dimensions. Remains subordinate per knowledge/ux/reading-contract.md.
acceptance: Classification Region presents a Factor / Score / Reason table (or equivalent compact tabular packaging) for classification signals.
Each displayed row/signal shows factor (or source), score, and reason when available.

Any compact score visualization (e.g. gauge) is Classification packaging only — it must not become an Overall Assessment / Overall Score / Synthesis rollup that replaces Regime/Risk/Economic/Exposure peers.
Classification remains compact and visually subordinate / adjacent to Analysis — not equal prominence.
Classification is not nested as an Analysis-owned Region inside Assessments.
Surface uses `@maguer/market-data-brand` Table/Card/Text (and related) primitives and tokens only.
User-facing labels and reasons come from locale / Content-resolved copy — no hardcoded designed English in components.
